selection.explanation:
All three candidates pass the basic tests and implement the core CommonMark inline Markdown algorithm. The key differentiator is architectural soundness and implementation completeness.

n5 uses explicit tokenization of the entire input (including delimiter runs as separate tokens with position tracking), then processes emphasis matches. This approach is cleaner and easier to reason about since positions are always relative to the original text.

n4 and n3 share identical visible code: they parse code spans and escapes first, leaving emphasis delimiters embedded in text items, then scan through text items to find delimiter runs and their flanking context. Both appear functionally correct in their logic for flanking rules and mod-3 matching.

The main observable difference is line count: n5 adds 331 lines, n4 adds 315 lines, and n3 adds 289 lines. All three diffs truncate at approximately the same point (after delimiter matching), so the full HTML rendering code is not shown. However, n4's extra 26 lines compared to n3 suggests a potentially more complete or robust implementation of the rendering phase, particularly since n3 and n4 have identical code in all visible portions.

n5's cleaner tokenization architecture—keeping position information throughout and explicitly representing all token types—is architecturally superior and less prone to subtle bugs in context tracking across items. The additional lines likely represent more comprehensive helper functions and rendering logic.

n4 likely has better rendering completeness than n3 given its additional code, though without seeing the truncated portions this cannot be verified.
